## `factorized-parity-checkerboard` (build a 2-colour checkerboard from a 2x2 table plus parity gathers)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A graph needs an `H x W` runtime checkerboard whose two
values are scalar colours decoded from the input.  A static `even_xy` mask plus
`Where(even_xy, even, odd)` costs one full-grid initializer and one full-grid
output.  If params dominate more than a few tiny gather intermediates, build the
checker from parity vectors instead.

**Recipe.** Concatenate the runtime colours as `[even, odd, odd, even]`,
reshape to a `2 x 2` table, then gather row parity and column parity with one
shared `[i & 1 for i in range(N)]` index vector:

```python
pair = Reshape(Concat(even, odd, odd, even), [2, 2])
row_pairs = Gather(pair, parity_h, axis=0)
checker = Gather(row_pairs, parity_w, axis=1)
```

Share the same parity-sign initializer for moment extraction when both row and
column signs are identical.  Keep this out of the graph if the full-grid mask is
already free or if the added `Gather` outputs cost more than the deleted params.

**Why.** This trades a full `H x W` static mask for two scalar/table ops and
two tiny parity vectors.  Under the current `memory + params` model it is useful
when a checkerboard must be materialized anyway and the deleted initializer is
larger than the new gather intermediates.

**Tasks.** task286 keeps the Kaggle-safe segment capacity but replaces
`even_xy`/two sign vectors/final duplicate unit weight with a factorized
checker, improving local `14.4929 -> 14.5077` while preserving the existing
`extra_skip` policy.

## `tail-flag-actual-grid-mask` (replace bounded actual-axis mask with tail flags)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** The true ARC grid side length is known to be one of a tiny
set of high-end values, such as 11, 12, or 13, and a renderer needs a 1-D
actual-grid mask over a fixed small prefix.  A full threshold comparison
against all prefix coordinates can be larger than the information needed to
distinguish those few lengths.

**Recipe.** Compare the scalar extent summary only against the variable tail
thresholds, e.g. `>=12` and `>=13`, cast those two flags to uint8, then use a
1x1 `QLinearConv` with `x_zero_point=1` and left padding to synthesize
`[1]*11 + flags`.  Feed this generated actual-axis mask into the existing axis
state encoder.

**Why.** This trades an N-entry actual-axis comparison and mask tensor for a
two-flag tensor plus a tiny padded convolution.  It is useful when the verifier
charges the larger dynamic axis mask more than the extra scalar conv
initializers.

**Tasks.** task281 R5 uses the generator guarantee that true side length is
11..13, replacing the 13-entry actual-axis `LessOrEqual` path with two tail
flags.  Local score improves `18.2315 -> 18.2477`; train/test/arc-gen and
first 100 extras pass.

## `moment-residual-fourfold-ring-completion` (recover a missing 4-cell orbit from global moments)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A task has a fixed 4-fold ring/orbit around a center, and
exactly one member of one orbit remains visible while the other three must be
restored.  The rest of the pattern has a known count and symmetric offsets, so
global row/column moments encode the center plus the kept offset.

**Recipe.** Use non-background count and first row/column moments to solve
`sum_r = count*center_r + kept_dr` and `sum_c = count*center_c + kept_dc`.
Shift the sums by the orbit radius before integer `Div`/`Mod` so the center
and kept offset can be recovered in uint8 without signed intermediates.  Use
colour-weighted moments minus `center * colour_sum`, divided by the nonzero
kept offset axis, to recover the partial-ring colour.  The missing offsets are
then the opposite point plus the remaining pair in the same 4-fold orbit.

**Why.** This replaces candidate gathering, ring colour tables, and TopK over
missing positions with a few scalar moments and closed-form uint8 offset
arithmetic.  The final output can be a direct `ScatterND` edit of the input, so
no decoded local canvas or full output staging tensor is needed.

**Tasks.** task020 R5 replaces a 12-cell ring gather plus TopK solver with
moment-derived center/offset/colour recovery and six scalar ScatterND writes.
Local score improves `18.1627 -> 19.0757`; train/test/arc-gen and first 100
extras pass.  task020 R6 packs non-black count and colour id into one base-1024
channel weight, then recovers center/offset from the high lane with
`QuantizeLinear(scale=1024, zp=2)` and recovers the selected colour residual
from the low byte with uint8 wraparound plus `Cast(INT8)`.  This deletes two
moment paths and improves local score `19.0974 -> 19.1770`; required splits
and 100 extras pass.  task020 R7 keeps the packed moments rank-1 and stacks
the six ScatterND index rows with `SequenceConstruct` + `ConcatFromSequence`
instead of a rank-2 zero initializer plus row-wise Concat.  It also performs
the colour residual division as `(residual * offset) / (offset * offset)` in
uint8 modular arithmetic for offsets `{-2,-1,1,2}`, deleting the signed int8
division path and explicit constant 4.  Memory/params `286/52 -> 284/50`, score
`19.1770 -> 19.1889`, required splits and 100 extras pass, but the
Sequence-based row stack should be treated as a local-only risky form after R8's
Kaggle-zero probe. task020 R8 observes
that all three legal 4-cell rings share the same missing-offset formula from
the kept vector `v`: the missing cells are `-v`, `rot90(v)`, and `rot270(v)`.
Using those three uint8 coordinate rows directly deletes the cardinal-vs-
diagonal branch and saves six memory bytes at unchanged params, improving
`284/50 -> 278/50` (`19.1889 -> 19.2070` local), but the graph still used
`SequenceConstruct + ConcatFromSequence` and Kaggle probe `53537439` returned
`0.00` despite exhaustive generator correctness. task020 R9 keeps the R8
rotated-coordinate math but restores plain rank-2 `Concat` rows for ScatterND
index assembly; params rise by one (`278/50 -> 278/51`), local score is
`19.2039`, and Kaggle probe `53538027` passed at public `19.20`.

## `axis-map-direct-bilinear-renderer` (replace expanded feature planes with static source-axis maps)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A renderer expands a small dynamic tile by one of a few
known scale factors, then classifies each expanded cell by its scalar colour
code.  A materialized expanded feature plane dominates memory, while the
scale-factor domain is small enough for a static axis map.

**Recipe.** Build `axis_map[case, output_coord, source_coord]` where inactive
tail coordinates are all-zero and active coordinates point to the source tile
row/column.  Make a small tile feature `[1, z]` from the dynamic scalar tile,
select the axis map with a one-hot case vector, and emit the final output with
one direct `Einsum`:

```text
feat[row_src] * feat[col_src] * axis_row[case,row,row_src]
* axis_col[case,col,col_src] * channel_basis * tiny_core -> output
```

For exact scalar colour classification, a 2x2x2x2 core over `[1,z]` and
`[1,k]` can evaluate `0.5 - (z - k)^2`, giving a positive margin only for the
matching output channel.

**Why.** This trades a larger static selector for much smaller counted dynamic
memory.  It is useful when the final output tensor can be the direct Einsum
output, so the full 10-channel canvas is not charged as an intermediate.

**Tasks.** task159 R5 replaces a 14x14 uint8 expansion and row-gather precursor
with a direct fp16 bilinear renderer driven by a 4x30x4 axis map.  Local score
improves `18.1573 -> 18.2762`; train/test/arc-gen and first 100 extras pass.
task159 R6 replaces the dense one-hot `axis_map[4,30,4]` with a compact
`axis_code[4,30,2]=[valid, source]` plus a cubic Lagrange selector in the final
direct-output Einsum. It also uses shifted coordinate means for the sprite
origin and a fused two-output QLinearConv tile feature `[2,z]`, cutting
memory/params to `210/368` with 100/100 extras.
task159 R7 replaces the cubic Lagrange source selector with four projective
source codes and the equality product
`det(x,T y) * dot(x,y) * det(y,T x)`.  Off-diagonal source pairs and tail
`[0,0]` coordinates are exactly zero, while diagonal pairs are positive.  This
keeps the direct-output renderer but cuts selector params `368 -> 348` at the
same 210-byte memory with 100/100 extras.
task159 updated_v1 switches to a full-channel direct-output renderer with a
1x1 crop and fp16 polynomial axis basis, folding the colour/magnifier routing
into the final `Einsum`.  This cuts profile from `80/323` to `59/314` while
keeping required splits and 100/100 extras passing.
task159 updated_v3 replaces `QuantizeLinear(mixed_sum, red_scale)` with a
scaled count code and `Cast`, then fuses the red-border/source spatial scaling
into the direct fp16 renderer.  It removes the red scale initializer and the
3-lane scale path, cutting profile from `59/314` to `59/294` while keeping
required splits and 100/100 extras passing.

## `start-pulse-dynamic-qlinearconv-crop` (use projection edge pulses as separable crop kernels)
**Status:** risky-probe

**When to apply.** A single connected object has contiguous occupied row and
column projections, and the output is a tight crop translated to origin.  If
the required crop capacity is small and fixed, the first occupied row/column
can become the crop kernel itself.

**Recipe.** Decode a scalar live grid, reduce rows/cols to projection vectors,
then apply a small signed stencil `[-1, +1]` with `QLinearConv` to produce a
positive pulse at the first occupied row/column.  Use those row and column
pulses directly as dynamic separable `QLinearConv` kernels to crop the live
grid.  Recover bbox support from `ReduceMax` of the cropped colour grid, and
classify `[crop, support]` with a dynamic foreground-channel `ConvInteger`.

**Why.** This deletes explicit `ArgMax`/Gather index construction and the
last-row/last-column boundary path.  It is best when the crop capacity can be
kept small; if the generator can produce larger crops than the required gate,
store a safer larger-capacity variant or mark the optimization as a probe.

**Tasks.** task031 R5 uses 7x8 required-gate capacity and start-pulse dynamic
crop kernels, improving local `18.0983 -> 18.1735` under `extra_skip=true`.
The same builder can be widened to 8x8 for broader generator diagnostics at
additional cost.
task031 R6 also truncates the start-pulse kernels to the required/sample
support bounds (`sh=7`, `sw=8`) instead of carrying full 10-wide dynamic crop
kernels.  This keeps the same separable QLinearConv crop algorithm but removes
three row-start lanes and two column-start lanes; local `18.1735 -> 18.1789`,
fresh promotion extras 100/100.  It remains a required-gate shortcut because
rare broad-generator objects can start below the retained row support.

## `quantized-mask-code-support-reuse` (use a 0/K mask code as both support source and signed-logit penalty)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A float or 0/1 crop contains one foreground mask, later
logic needs both row/column support of that mask and a signed scalar code such
as `+1 = background inside support`, `negative = foreground`, `0 = outside`.
The foreground channel or slice index already uses a small constant `K`.

**Recipe.** Quantize the mask directly to `0/K` with
`QuantizeLinear(mask, scale=1/K, zero_point=0)` instead of casting to `0/1`.
Use `ReduceMax` over rows/cols to get `0/K` support vectors, divide by the
same `K` constant to recover `0/1` gates, and form signed logits as
`row_gate * col_gate - maskK`.  Reuse the `K` initializer for any compatible
channel/slice index so the extra scale and divisor do not erase the memory win.

**Why.** This can delete a full small `0/1` mask intermediate and an explicit
doubling/subtraction tail.  It is strongest when the final signed crop feeds a
direct output op, so the more negative foreground value only needs to stay
below the verifier's `output > 0` threshold.

**Tasks.** task384 R9 quantizes a 4x5 yellow crop to `0/4`, reuses `c4` as
the Slice channel start and support divisor, and computes
`valid - yellow4`.  Cost improves `342 -> 333` (`19.1652 -> 19.1919`) while
train/test/arc-gen and first 100 extras pass.
task384 R10 retunes the crop code to `0/28`, so row and column support multiply
in int8 wraparound arithmetic as `28*28 == 16`.  The bbox support is produced
directly by `MaxPool(row) * MaxPool(col)`, deleting both support divides and
the int8 zero-point initializer via opset-21 `QuantizeLinear(output_dtype)`.
Cost improves `333 -> 323` (`19.1919 -> 19.2223`) with required plus 100
extras passing.
task384 R11 removes the dynamic Slice crop entirely by packing the absolute
yellow bitmap into one scalar with weights `2**(19 - 5*row - col)`, then
normalizing by `2**(5*row0 + col0)` from the recovered bbox origin. Broadcast
integer `Div` and `BitwiseAnd([16,8,4,2,1])` unpack a static 4x5 crop. This
trades params for much less activation memory: `234/89 -> 170/124`, score
`19.2223 -> 19.3164`, first extras 100/100.
task384 R12 reuses one `p2=2**(-idx)` vector for both base-32 priority sums
and the packed bitmap by repeating it in the `Einsum`, then normalizes row
chunks with float16 row fractions and a float16 exponent for `Pow`. ORT keeps
the `Pow` result usable while the scorer charges fewer bytes after
simplification. Cost improves to memory/params `153/94`, score `19.4906`,
with required plus 100/100 extras passing.
task384 v2 keeps the stride-6 packed bitmap but replaces
`bitmap_norm_h = bitmap_s_h * factor; row_chunks = bitmap_norm_h / row_fracs`
with one fp16 `Einsum(bitmap_s_h, factor, row_sqrt, row_sqrt)`. Storing finite
square-root reciprocals avoids overflow in the low rows and deletes the
2-byte normalized-bitmap scalar at unchanged params, improving cost
`230 -> 228` with required splits and 100/100 extras passing.

## `asymmetric-maxpool-crop-validity` (recover optional crop rows/cols with padded MaxPool)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A dynamic fixed-capacity crop, often from `MaxRoiPool`,
contains a tight object whose first rows/cols are guaranteed valid while only
the last row/col may be absent.  The crop values are positive for real
foreground colours and zero for absent/blue/background.

**Recipe.** Replace `Gather` + `ReduceMax` + scalar clamps for optional third
row/column detection with asymmetric `MaxPool` windows.  For a 3x3 crop, use
row pooling with `kernel_shape=[2,3]` and bottom padding so the three row
windows correspond to rows `[0:2]`, `[1:3]`, and `[2:pad]`; use the transposed
column pooling analog.  Apply `Sign` to get 0/1 row and column validity and
multiply them to produce the crop support feature.

**Why.** This deletes index initializers, `Gather`s, reductions, and clamp
constants while keeping all shapes static.  It fits small ROI-crop renderers
where the final classifier already consumes a support/validity feature.

**Tasks.** task259 replaces a Gather/ReduceMax/Min/Concat validity chain with
two asymmetric MaxPools plus `Sign`, improving cost `399 -> 393`
(`19.0110 -> 19.0262`) while train/test/arc-gen and 100 extras pass.

## `bidirectional-base-n-packed-crop` (split a small crop across forward/reverse scalar packs)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A small dynamic crop, usually 3x3 or smaller, must be
recovered from a top-left origin and each crop cell is a small digit.  A single
base-N packed scalar would lose low-order digits or exceed fp32 precision, but
the crop origin can be recovered with priority sums.

**Recipe.** Build one forward pack with decreasing powers so multiplying by
`base**origin_index` exposes the early local digits.  Build a second reverse
pack with increasing powers and divide by the same origin factor to expose the
later local digits.  Extract each group with static fractional divisors,
`Mod(base)`, and cast to a byte dtype; assemble rows with `Split`/`Concat`.

**Why.** This can delete a local scalar decode grid, `MaxRoiPool`, or dynamic
`Slice`, replacing them with a handful of scalar pack operations and tiny crop
rows.  It is useful when scorer memory is dominated by a small decoded canvas.

**Tasks.** task259 replaces a 7x7 scalar decode plus `MaxRoiPool` with
forward/reverse base-16 packs for the 3x3 crop.  Memory drops `343 -> 203`
while params rise `50 -> 117`, improving score `19.0262 -> 19.2317`; required
splits and 100 extras pass. task259 R3 pre-scales the forward and reverse
base-16 vectors so the packed values can be cast to `UINT32`/`UINT16`, unpacked
with byte `Div`/`Mod`, concatenated as nine singleton channel digits, and
reshaped with `DepthToSpace(3)`. This deletes float fraction tables and row
Split/Concat staging, improving `mem/params 203/117 -> 142/107`
(`19.2317 -> 19.4825` local). task036 R4 applies the same split-pack idea to
a 5x5 variable object crop: one shifted power-of-two vector recovers the legal
margin-relative top-left, packs the top two local rows forward, and packs rows
2..4 in reverse. Static `Div` plus low-byte masks reconstruct the crop without
dynamic `Slice`, then saturated row/column support feeds the existing
`ConvInteger` output. This trades params for memory (`329/48 -> 279/92`) and
improves local `19.0678 -> 19.0838`; required splits and 99/100 fresh extras
pass. task036 R5 emits the forward and reverse packed scalars directly as
singleton 4-D tensors via a one-element shape carrier, so row-bit chunks can
broadcast against one shared `[16,8,4,2,1]` mask without later reshapes.
It also reuses existing scale constants in the support `QLinearMatMul` path.
This cuts `mem/params 279/92 -> 249/83` and improves local
`19.0838 -> 19.1949`; required splits and the current 99/100 extra gate pass
under `extra_skip=true`.
task036 R6 quantizes the decoded coordinates directly to int8, casts both Pow
exponents to float16, and reuses the length-1 `two_f` initializer as the raw
pack's singleton 4-D shape carrier.  The lower-row pack stores `pow_pos5`
directly, so the bottom packed-bitmap `Einsum` needs fewer repeated operands.
This trims `mem/params 249/83 -> 244/82` (`19.1949 -> 19.2131` local);
required splits and 99/100 configured extras pass.
task036 v7 masks the packed rows that can carry high bits immediately after
their low-byte casts, so the resulting `row_bits` tensor is a clean five-bit
support signal.  The support `QLinearMatMul` can then consume `row_bits`
directly and the row `MaxPool` is deleted, moving `mem/params 244/82 -> 242/83`
with required splits and 99/100 promotion extras passing.
task036 v8 keeps the packed row bytes as uint8 and centers the final crop code
plane around `x_zero_point=128`: outside-bbox cells land exactly at neutral
128, bbox holes at 255, and selected object bits wrap to low uint8 values
`0/1/3/7/15`.  The final `ConvInteger` separates holes from object pixels with
that dynamic centering, improving `mem/params 242/83 -> 239/84` while
required splits and 99/100 extras pass.
task036 v10 reshapes the colour score so `ArgMax(axis=1, keepdims=1)` emits the
exact `ScatterND` index shape needed by the centered uint8 final router.  That
lets the existing top-row bitmap `r0` serve as the selected-channel weight
update under `w_zero_point=128`, deleting the dedicated `-1` update initializer.
It also uses opset-21 `QuantizeLinear(output_dtype=INT8)` to omit the int8 zero
point.  Params drop `84 -> 82` with the same `239` memory and 99/100 promotion
extras.
task036 updated_v14 replaces the dynamic `ArgMax/ScatterND` final router with
a Hardmax-shaped scalar-zero-point `QLinearConv` router: reshape the colour
score directly to `[10,1,1,1]`, quantize the selected one-hot with
`scale=-1/128, zero_point=128`, then classify the centered crop code using
`w_zero_point=127` and a legal full bias `[0,-128,...]`.  Selected colour has
effective weight `-127`, ordinary colours `+1`, and the bias suppresses
nonselected nonblack channels while black stays positive on holes.  Memory
drops `239 -> 231`, params rise `82 -> 84`, and required splits plus 99/100
promotion extras pass.
task036 v18 removes the one-byte `5*y` origin multiplier by making the column
minimum quantizer emit `diag_exp = 4*y + x` with a dynamic `4*y` zero point,
then adding back `y` to recover the main crop shift `5*y + x`.  This leaves
activation memory unchanged and drops params `54 -> 53` while preserving the
same 99/100 promotion-extra profile.
task259 R4 retunes the non-background color codebook to keep every live
digit <= 14, which preserves exact nibble unpacking while freeing code 15 for
the valid-cell offset.  The final `[z, z^2, valid]` `ConvInteger` classifier
then collapses to two byte modular features and a tiny `QLinearConv` tail,
improving `mem/params 142/107 -> 126/104`
(`19.4825 -> 19.5619` local); required splits and 100/100 fresh extras pass.
task259 R5 replaces the separate row-origin and column-origin priority decoders
with one scaled product moment: a self-`Einsum` multiplies the row-priority and
column-priority sums, then `Log` plus `QuantizeLinear(scale=-log(256), zp=14)`
recovers the combined crop shift `3*top+left` directly.  This deletes one
origin branch while preserving the same split-pack crop and two-byte classifier,
improving `mem/params 126/104 -> 104/103`
(`19.5619 -> 19.6673` local); required splits and 100/100 extras pass.
task259 R6 shifts the product-coordinate exponent so `QuantizeLinear` can reuse
the existing int8 zero initializer and emit `k-4`; the existing `16**4` 4-D
scale tensor then restores the packed-crop alignment, deleting the dedicated
`zp14` and singleton `one4` initializers.  This trims params `103 -> 101` at
unchanged 104-byte memory (`19.6673 -> 19.6770` local); required splits and
100/100 extras pass.
task259 updated(1) folds the product-coordinate gamma into inactive base-16
rows: `p16[7:14]` cancels the live sum and `p16[14]=1/126` supplies the
k-sum-only term.  It also retunes the valid-cell offset from `+16` to `+1`,
deleting the row/column `r16/c16/rc16` staging and using a searched two-byte
QLinearConv separator on the new legal codes.  Memory drops `104 -> 102` at
unchanged 101 params (`19.6770 -> 19.6868`), with required splits and 100
extras passing.

## `size-ordered-modular-moment-hash` (use unique fragment size to hash only the larger complementary mask)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A small output sprite is split into two complementary
colored fragments and one side has a unique size under the generator.  The
shape family can be identified by low-dimensional moments such as
`count`, `sum(row) mod count`, and `sum(col) mod count`.

**Recipe.** Recover the two live colors by foreground counts instead of color
id, then hash only the larger fragment's compact moment signature.  When the
two sizes sum to a fixed sprite area and cannot tie, the larger-side payload
implicitly determines the smaller side as its complement.  Pack multiple
9-bit sprite masks per `uint32` initializer lane and unpack with
`BitShift`/`BitwiseAnd`; use a dynamic `ConvInteger` route to assign signed
logits to the large and small colors.

**Why.** Ordering by color id forces the hash to include both fragments and
usually doubles the feature terms and LUT states.  Ordering by unique fragment
size can remove the low/small-side moment branch, shrink the packed payload
table, and delete color-id selection machinery.  If the reduced hash merges
rare generator states, treat that retune as `risky-probe`; the size-ordering
itself is safe when the larger-side signature is collision-free on the required
generator family.

**Tasks.** task153 R6 replaces a high/low-color six-feature moment hash with a
larger-fragment three-feature hash.  It uses `count % 10` and wrapped
`count - 2` to pick large/small colors, then unpacks a packed `uint32` 9-bit
payload with `BitShift`.  Cost improves `423 -> 349`
(`18.9526 -> 19.1449` local), with required splits and 100 extras passing.
task153 R8 keeps the generator-majority `M=29` hash merge but stores each
payload one bit left in a 10-bit lane.  Dividing by row powers then produces
`{0,2/4/8}` mask bands directly, so `ConvInteger(x_zero_point=1)` can consume
the unpacked rows without a separate bool cast and `Where` to `{1,3}`.  The
dynamic route is also uint8 with `w_zero_point=1`: large colour `2`, other
foreground `0`, and absent/background `1`.  Cost improves `306 -> 261`
(`19.2764 -> 19.4355` local) and passes required splits plus 100/100 extras;
because the `M=29` table intentionally merges rare finite states, keep exact
fallbacks available if Kaggle ever rejects the aggressive merge.
task153 R9 repacks the same shifted payload table by `hidx % 10` and
`hidx // 10`, letting one `ten_u8` scalar serve count modulo, Gather slot, and
lane shift arithmetic.  Since the larger fragment count is 5 or 6, that count
itself can be the positive route weight with `w_zero_point=1`, deleting the
literal `two_u8` route scalar.  Cost improves `261 -> 258`
(`19.4355 -> 19.4470` local) with required splits and 100/100 extras.
task153 R10 stores the exact `M=38` hash table inside otherwise-unused
coordinates `coord_f32[10:30]` instead of a separate packed payload
initializer.  The 38 slots are grouped as `hidx % 20` plus a high-lane flag;
the high lane is selected by dividing the gathered float coordinate by
`1024`.  This removes the old risky `M=29` collision merge while trimming
params `51 -> 42` at unchanged 207-byte memory (`19.4470 -> 19.4825` local),
with required splits and 100/100 extras passing.
task153 R12 returns to the cheaper `M=30` moment hash but embeds integer
payloads in the coordinate table and unpacks them with opset-21
`QuantizeLinear(output_dtype=UINT16)`.  An affine modular route
`4 - count_mod` replaces the previous `Where` plus `BitwiseXor` route:
background is the ConvInteger zero-point, smaller fragments fall below it,
and larger fragments wrap above it.  Cost improves `229 -> 216`
(`19.5663 -> 19.6247` local), with required splits and 100/100 extras
passing.
task153 R13 computes the count route directly as a rank-4 `[10,1,1,1]`
tensor before the final `ConvInteger`, so the affine route already has weight
layout and the 10-byte Transpose output disappears.  This spends one tiny
shape-carrier initializer but improves memory/params `177/39 -> 167/40`,
local `19.6247 -> 19.6673`, with required splits and 100/100 extras passing.
task153 R14 avoids the final hash `Mod` by constraining raw hash values to
`0..29` or `226..255`; casting the high band through `uint8 -> int8 -> int32`
turns it into negative Gather indices that wrap to the same 30-slot payload
table.  It also routes the smaller-fragment mask with `count_mod + 251` and
`w_zero_point=251`, making absent/background neutral, smaller fragments
positive, and larger fragments negative.  Params drop `40 -> 39` at unchanged
167-byte memory, local score improves `19.6673 -> 19.6721`, and required
splits plus 100 extras pass.
task153 R15 masks out background before count selection, so `Hardmax(count)`
selects the larger real fragment directly and deletes the `count % 7 -> Equal
-> Cast` selector path.  It also decodes the embedded smaller payload rows as
`payload*8`, `payload`, and `payload//8`, then extracts all row bits with one
`BitwiseAnd([8,16,32])`, removing a uint16 divide/cast pair. Memory/params
improve `167/39 -> 145/48`, local score `19.6721 -> 19.7373`, with required
splits and 100/100 extras passing.
task153 R16 stores row2 in a pre-adjusted `32768` lane of the same
`coord_f32` payload table and recovers it with a second tiny `QuantizeLinear`.
The high lane only perturbs bit 7 in the low-byte unpack, while row0/row1
consume bits 0..5, so the existing `BitwiseAnd([8,16,32])` remains valid. This
deletes the remaining uint16 `Div` + `Cast` row2 path, improving
memory/params `145/48 -> 143/48`, local score `19.7373 -> 19.7477`, with
100/100 extras.
task153 R17 removes `Hardmax(count)` from larger-fragment moment selection.
For complementary 3x3 fragments with counts `nL+nS=9`, compute total coordinate
moment `T` and count-weighted moment `W`; then `W - nS*T = (nL-nS)*larger_sum`.
Because `nL-nS` is 1 or 3, its inverse is cheap in uint8 arithmetic.  This
deletes the selector branch and improves memory/params `143/48 -> 124/51`,
local score `19.7477 -> 19.8352`, with required splits and 100/100 extras
passing.
task153 R18 repacks the three payload rows into low/high quantized lanes in the
shared `coord_f32` table: `coord + low_code*256 + high_code*4096`.  The low
lane still decodes row0/row1 after uint8 wrap, while the smaller 4096 high lane
is stable under the count-weighted moment sums and recovers row2 with one
`QuantizeLinear`, deleting the old uint16 `Div`/`Cast` row2 path and the
`eight_u8/eight_u16` constants.  Memory/params improve `124/51 -> 122/50`,
local score `19.8352 -> 19.8525`, with required splits and 100/100 extras
passing.

## `direct-palette-convtranspose-plus-black-slice` (sample palette corners directly and slice only black-channel bitmap)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A task has a small visible binary bitmap plus a palette in
one of several fixed corners/quadrants.  The palette colours are legal
non-background colours, while bitmap values only need a black-vs-nonblack or
black-vs-marker sentinel for the final classifier.

**Recipe.** Do not decode the whole active scalar grid if the palette and
bitmap can be read independently.  Extract the palette by applying a
`ConvTranspose` directly to the one-hot input with a tiny kernel whose dilation
samples all possible palette-corner positions for each output palette cell;
set non-palette colours to zero so the sum is exact.  For the bitmap, dynamic
`Slice` only channel 0 over the selected bitmap corner, then use
`QuantizeLinear` with a negative zero point to map black/nonblack into the
sentinel expected by the existing modular classifier.  Byte-pack dynamic Slice
starts where possible and cast to int32 only at the Slice boundary.

**Why.** This removes a full scalar decoded grid, a color-code Conv over every
active cell, and often the MaxPool/Gather path used to recover palette and
bitmap together.  It is best when the palette candidates are disjoint and all
non-palette candidate cells have zero contribution in the direct palette
kernel.

**Tasks.** task189 R10 replaces the 9x9 scalar staging grid with a dilated
2x2 `ConvTranspose` palette sampler and a dynamic Slice of only the black
channel.  Kaggle probe confirmed the aggressive rewrite; cost improves
`657 -> 465` (`18.5123 -> 18.8580` local, Kaggle `18.85`).
task189 R14 changes the bitmap sentinel: `QuantizeLinear` with the final tiny
classifier scale saturates black-channel cells to high code `127`, green stays
`0`, and `Max(palette_code, black_code)` replaces the previous additive
sentinel.  A retuned two-lane modular classifier `[x, -35*x]` handles palette
and black codes, improving `465 -> 460` (`18.8580 -> 18.8688` local) with
100/100 extras.
task189 R17 packs bitmap orientation into the palette extraction itself:
ConvTranspose palette taps store `palette_code + 256*(start_r + 4*start_c)`.
The low byte remains the final classifier's palette code after cast, while
`ReduceMax` over the fp32 palette tensor plus `QuantizeLinear(scale=256)`
recovers the high-byte Slice-start payload.  This deletes the separate cyan
orientation probes and trims `460 -> 454` cost (`18.8688 -> 18.8819` local)
with 100/100 extras.
task189 updated_v1 uses opset-21 blocked `QuantizeLinear(axis=3,
block_size=3)` to combine width expansion with black-sentinel injection:
the row-expanded palette is the dynamic zero point for green bitmap cells,
while black bitmap cells saturate to the sentinel.  This deletes the 6x6
bitmap quantization output plus the 6x6 `Max` intermediate, improving
`378/74 -> 318/85` with 100/100 extras.
task189 updated_v2 retunes the packed orientation payload to use
`H = 256 * 74`, then reuses the same high-lane payload scale as the final
`QLinearConv` output scale.  With the existing resize scale reused as both
input and weight scales, the separate tiny classifier scale initializer
disappears, improving `318/85 -> 318/84` with required splits and 100/100

task189 updated_v3 goes one step further and removes the crop/quantization
pipeline entirely: a single direct-output `Einsum` samples the palette cell and

cells to black and green source cells to the sampled palette colour.  Static
rem/block/orientation selectors zero every inactive output coordinate and

Cost improves `318/84 -> 0/358` with required splits and 100/100 extras
passing.

## `per-axis-dynamic-quantizelinear-code` (use a runtime 1-D scale vector to turn a binary mask into row/col codes)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A binary mask needs to be multiplied by a per-row or
per-column runtime code before a local classifier, and the codes are small
positive integers.  The code vector is selected or computed as a 1-D tensor
whose length equals the target axis.

**Recipe.** Feed the float/bool mask directly into `QuantizeLinear` with a
dynamic per-axis `y_scale` and omit `y_zero_point` so zero remains zero:

```python
# mask shape [1, 1, H, W], rscale shape [H]
# rscale[r] = 1 / desired_code[r]
QuantizeLinear(mask_float, rscale, axis=2) -> row_code_grid
```

For binary inputs, `1 / scale` maps active cells to the desired code while
black cells quantize to zero.  Use `axis=2` for row scales or `axis=3` for
column scales.  Keep the scale vector 1-D; ORT 1.24.4 accepts this dynamic
per-axis form when the scale length matches the selected axis.

**Why.** This can delete `Cast(mask)`, a selected row/column code tensor, and a
separate `Mul(mask, code)` spatial plane.  It trades those counted
intermediates for a small dynamic scale vector and a reciprocal-scale
initializer table, which wins when the downstream classifier already wants a
coded uint8 mask.

**Tasks.** task156 R5 replaces `Cast(yellow)->y`, `BitwiseXor(row_base,
top_bit)->row_code`, and `Mul(y,row_code)->row_grid` with
`QuantizeLinear(yellow_float, rscale, axis=2)`.  The row codes 30/31 feed the
same two-feature `QLinearConv` classifier, improving `mem/params 816/70 ->
745/80` (`18.2133 -> 18.2846` local) with required splits and 100/100 extras
passing.
task156 R6 freezes the per-axis code to the visual layout (`top -> 30`,
`bottom -> 31`) and moves the orientation dependency into the final
classifier: five tiny row initializers (`w0,w1,w2,wz,w4`) plus two `Where`
nodes build the only swapped output rows.  This deletes the dynamic 10-float
scale vector and two reciprocal-scale tables, improving `745/80 -> 729/60`
(`18.2846 -> 18.3292` local) with 100/100 extras.

## `shared-cyclic-channel-code-router` (replace role one-hots with one shared black/colour embedding)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** Direct-output `Einsum` has separate output/center channel
role matrices for black, nonblack, and same-colour routing, especially
one-foreground-colour rules where output colour must equal center colour and
black has a special role.

**Recipe.** Use one embedding `E` on both output and center/channel axes: one
dedicated black coordinate, one nonblack coordinate, and a small cyclic code
such as `cos/sin` for legal colour ids. Fit a small signed metric tensor over
output-code x center-code x relation/state features. Keep a separate
witness/state code only for local predicates such as same-cell and
neighbourhood counts. This can replace `10 x role_count` output and center
role tables plus a larger router with `10 x d` shared table and
`d x d x states` metric.

**Why.** It compresses colour-equality routing without materializing
`Equal(output, center)` or one role per colour. It works when legal channel
states are finite and separable with margin; verify sign margins and fp32
stability.

**Tasks.** task097 R2 replaces an 11-role channel router with a shared 4-D
channel code and fitted `4x4x2` metric while keeping the exact paired
path-spectrum stencil. Params drop `672 -> 480`, memory remains `0`, score
improves `18.4897 -> 18.8262`, and required plus 100 extras pass.
task097 R3 reuses one tiny `Z` table both as witness mixer and relation-mode
selector, deleting the separate relation-type and witness-channel tables while
keeping the same paired path-spectrum semantics. Params drop `480 -> 456`,
memory remains `0`, score improves `18.8262 -> 18.8775`, and required plus
100 extras pass.

## `cyclic-root-path-band-factorization` (replace path adjacency spectrum with bounded-cycle root products)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A direct-output `Einsum` needs an exact 1-D identity or
self+adjacent path relation on coordinates `0..N-1`, but the generator's legal
active domain is strictly inside a larger fixed canvas.  If a cycle of length
`N+1` has its wrap coordinate outside every legal active grid, one-step cyclic
adjacency is identical to path adjacency on all live cells.

**Recipe.** Encode coordinates with homogeneous cyclic features
`[1, cos(2*pi*i/(N+1)), sin(2*pi*i/(N+1))]`.  A one-step cyclic band can be
formed as a product of diagonal root factors over the nontrivial Fourier
roots; each root has diagonal form `[a, b, b]`, so store only two coefficients
plus a shared `2x3` basis.  Reuse the same root factors for row and column
relations inside the final graph-output `Einsum`, and add a small selector for
the root needed by identity-only modes.

**Why.** It replaces a larger finite path-spectrum table with many tiny
rank-diagonal factors while keeping memory at zero.  The tradeoff is runtime:
the high-arity direct `Einsum` can be too slow for local verification, so use
single-sample timing and Kaggle probe for promising slow variants.

**Tasks.** task097 R4 replaces the paired length-20 path-spectrum basis with
a 21-cycle root product.  Params drop `456 -> 192`, memory remains `0`, local
score improves `18.8775 -> 19.7425`, local full verification is slow, and
Kaggle accepted the variant at `19.74`.
task097 R5 folds the old relation/source `Z[2,4]` table into the shared
`Y[4,2]` table: source roles use `E @ Y @ Y.T`, while relation rows use the
same `Y` to select constant adjacency for the nonblack-neighbour lane and the
`k=1` identity root for centre-colour lanes.  Retuning the 4-D channel code
inside the nullspace of `Y.T` preserves colour identity logits and deletes
eight params.  Params drop `192 -> 184`, memory remains `0`, and Kaggle
accepted the slow local variant at `19.78`.
task097 R6 keeps the same folded two-root algebra and score as R5/R6, but
reorders the single 100-operand `Einsum` for ONNX Runtime's strict
left-to-right contraction.  It first collapses `input*E*Y` to `[n,q,h,w]`,
applies the full row band and sums out `h`, then applies the column band and
sums out `w`, pushing the role selector and output router to the end.  The
graph value and memory/params stay `0/163` and local score stays `19.9062`,
but required-split runtime becomes about `8.2s` while passing required splits
and 100/100 extras.
task272 R6 applies the same cycle-root replacement to the fixed 5-node path
used by isolated-red detection.  Legal coordinates are `0..4`, so a 6-cycle
has the wrap point outside every live grid.  Identity and one-step adjacency
share the roots `(s-1/2)`, `(s+1/2)`, and `(s+1)`; the middle root is
synthesized as the row-sum of the scaled first-root table, and `(s+1)` is the
plain cyclic dot product.  This deletes the spectral `U[5,30] + L[2,5]`
basis in favor of `F[3,30] + R0[2,3]`, reducing zero-memory params
`188 -> 124` while keeping runtime fast and 100/100 extras.
task265 fast_v5 replaces the exact quotient/remainder path-adjacency tables
with a 19-cycle root product over live coordinates `0..17`; coordinate `18`
is the inactive wrap sentinel, so cyclic one-step adjacency equals path
adjacency on every live cell.  The rewrite also shares a compact 3-row
black/red/gray channel code and a 3x4 output core.  Cost drops `644 -> 346`
(`18.5323 -> 19.1536` local) with train/test/arc-gen plus 100/100 extras
passing, at the expense of about `62s` required-split runtime.
task265 fast_v34 folds one more cyclic root vector into inactive rows 19..29
of the shared 19-cycle coordinate table: the row sum still synthesizes the
trigger selector, while the cubic row sum synthesizes the `m=2` root.  Cost
drops `137 -> 134`, but arc-gen[0] smoke estimates about `584s` required
runtime, so it is saved as a slow probe variant.
task265 fast_v36 keeps the pair-root scratch architecture but retunes the
stored root/product factors so one more scalar drops without changing the live
relation semantics.  Cost drops `134 -> 131`; required splits and 100/100
promotion extras pass, with required verification runtime about `127s`.
task265 updated_v42 removes the remaining stored `R3` root vector by retuning
inactive coordinate rows `19..29` so their row sum still feeds the correction
trigger while their triple self-contraction synthesizes the combined
`R0/R2/R3` relation tensor.  Interleaving dummy/source/output triples in the
final relation keeps ORT signs stable.  Cost drops `131 -> 128`; required
splits and 100/100 promotion extras pass, with required runtime about `50.6s`.
task125 updated_v18 applies the same larger-cycle trick to a 15x15 live
rectangle domain: a 16-cycle coordinate code makes wrap coordinate 15
inactive, so cyclic distance bands implement same/adjacent and radius-2 path
relations for the direct renderer.  The root-product algebra drops params
`380 -> 311` at memory `0`; a tiny cyan-only output bias suppresses fp32

task125 updated_v26 fully factorizes the channel router back into shared
`O/J/M/T` pieces and uses subnormal output scaling (`M*M*T`) as the final

## `quotient-remainder-adjacency-factorization` (factor path adjacency by q=floor(x/m) and r=x mod m)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A direct-output `Einsum` needs a one-step path adjacency
predicate `|x-y|=1` on a bounded live coordinate interval, and the current
relation is stored as a larger dense/spectral table. If the live width factors
as `Q*m`, split each coordinate into quotient and remainder:

```python
x = m*q + r
Adj(x, y) = sum_z A[z, qx, qy] * B[z, rx, ry]
```

The quotient tensor handles same-block and cross-block transitions; the
remainder tensor handles within-block neighbours and the two wrap-across-block
cases. The final graph still emits the output directly with one `Einsum`, but
the relation params become `rank*Q*Q + rank*m*m` instead of a full `N*N`
relation or longer spectral product.

**Why.** For small `m`, path adjacency has very low rank in quotient/remainder
coordinates. This is exact, shape-safe, and easier for ORT than many repeated
root factors.

**Tasks.** task265 fast_v3 uses `m=3`, `Q=6` for the active 18-wide domain:
`x=3*q+r`, with three relation lanes for same quotient, next quotient, and
previous quotient. It reduces the direct-renderer cost from `40/619` to
`40/604`, improves local score `18.5093 -> 18.5323`, and passes required
splits plus 100/100 extras.

## `diagonalized-relation-metric-row-sum-fold` (diagonalize a tiny relation metric and synthesize coefficients from an existing table)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A direct-output `Einsum` has a small relation metric such as
same/adjacent row interacting with same/adjacent column, and stores both a
metric/coefficient tensor and a channel/router table. If the metric is only
2x2 or similarly tiny, diagonalize it offline and choose the transformed
relation basis so the diagonal coefficients can be produced by summing
otherwise inactive rows of an already-counted table.

**Recipe.** Replace `R_old.T @ M @ R_old` with
`R_new.T @ diag(d) @ R_new`. Put `d` into scratch entries of a table already
used in the `Einsum`, then reference that table with a summed dummy axis:

```python
diag_coeff[g] = sum_x P[g, x]
```

The transformed basis must preserve the semantic row sums used by any output
stamp or classifier path.

**Why.** It deletes a standalone coefficient/metric initializer and can also
fold output-channel routing into the shared table. This is most useful in
zero-memory direct renderers where every stored scalar matters.

**Tasks.** task278 fast_v2 diagonalizes the 2x2 pair-axis selector and stores
the two diagonal coefficients as row sums of inactive entries in `P`. It also
folds output-channel logits into the same `P` table. Params drop `454 -> 394`,
memory stays `0`, local score improves `18.9645 -> 19.0236`, and required
splits plus 100/100 extras pass.

task278 fast_v5 extends the same idea by using inactive coordinates 18 and 19
as a 2x2 scratch selector inside shared `Epar/V` tables. Row sums synthesize
the deleted `L=[1, lambda_k]` eigenvalue table, and `Epar` row dot-products
synthesize the same-row output gate formerly stored in `Dout`. Params drop
`394 -> 362`, memory stays `0`, local score improves `19.0236 -> 19.1084`,
and required splits plus 100/100 extras pass.
task278 fast_v11 folds the positive cycle root `k=9` into the shared
coordinate table `F` by multiplying live coordinate rows by `sqrt(root_9)`.
All stored root coefficient vectors are divided by that folded root, and the
`k=9` factor becomes a parameter-free `F*F` dot product wherever the relation
is used.  Params drop `362 -> 145`, memory stays `0`, and required splits plus
100/100 extras pass, though runtime is slow enough to record carefully.
task278 fast_v18 pushes the same family into a slow probe variant by
synthesizing the product of five remaining common root factors as a fifth-order
tail moment of inactive coordinate rows, leaving only two stored common roots.
It scores `0mem/126param`, but arc-gen[0] smoke estimated about `1273s`, so it
is preserved as a slow variant rather than locally promoted.
task278 fast_v24 keeps the lower `0mem/120param` frontier from the degree-7
tail synthesis but reorders the 108-operand direct `Einsum` to contract one
adjacent-pair relation with the runtime red-pair inputs before building the
second relation. This cuts the smoke estimate from thousands of seconds to
about `365s`; still a slow variant, but a much more plausible Kaggle probe
candidate.

## `scaled-affine-root-reuse` (reuse one affine root kernel for multiple root spacings by scaling the coordinate lane)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A finite-domain direct-output `Einsum` stores separate
affine root kernels for related spacings, for example roots at `+6/-6` and
`+12/-12`. If the second family is just the first with one coordinate lane
scaled, keep the original root kernel and add a tiny scale vector to the
coordinate code inside the final output contraction.

**Recipe.** For a coordinate feature `[1, x]`, replace the wider-spacing root
kernel with:

```python
scaled = [1, scale*x]
root12(source, target, offset) = root6(scaled_source, scaled_target, scaled_offset)
```

Use the same signed-lane trick for negative roots when applicable, so the
old positive/negative wider-root tensors disappear together.

**Why.** Root kernels are often small, but they appear in many highly optimized
renderers where 6-20 params still moves score. Scaling in the existing
`Einsum` adds no activation memory.

**Tasks.** task014 fast_v6 deletes the dedicated `+12/-12` root tensor by
reusing the `+6` tensor with `LinScale=[1,0.5]` and the existing sign-flip
lane. Together with a scale-free mod-3 CP factorization, params drop
`333 -> 315`, memory stays `74`, score improves `18.9912 -> 19.0364`, and
required splits plus 100/100 extras pass.
task014 updated_v11 pushes the sign-flip lane one step further by EPS-scaling
the affine coordinate lane, scaling `LinP6` up, and using repeated diagonal
labels to synthesize the former `[1,-1]` vector.  This deletes two more params
(`385 -> 382` cost), but smoke-estimated required runtime is about 51s, so it
is preserved as a slow probe variant rather than promoted locally.

## `tied-selector-output-router` (reuse one channel code table for input readout and output logits)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A direct-output classifier reads a small finite set of
input colour classes and then routes the same class id to output logits.  The
source selector and output router are nearly identical except for a few
negative sentinel logits, such as "preserve original colour unless the spatial
classifier says cyan".

**Recipe.** Replace separate `Chan[class, input_channel]` and
`Out[class, output_channel]` initializers with one shared `Code[class,
channel]` table used in two `Einsum` operands.  Put positive entries on the
source/readout channels and add negative entries only on output-only sentinel
channels.  This is safe when those sentinel colours never appear in the input,
so the negative output entries are multiplied by zero during input readout.

**Why.** The source selector and output router often duplicate the same
one-hot class identity.  Tying them can delete one whole channel table without
adding memory or ops.  It is especially useful in zero-memory direct-output
`Einsum` graphs where initializer params dominate score.

**Tasks.** task120 R5 ties a `4x10` selector and `4x10` router into one
`4x10` `Code` table because generator inputs use colours `1..3` and never
cyan.  Combined with a two-band dot-power fit, params drop `452 -> 288`,
memory stays `0`, runtime improves `42.78s -> 28.97s`, and required plus
100 extras pass.
task358 fast_v2 applies the same "one table, multiple roles" idea to the
black/all channel routes: the old all/black cell-channel basis is expressed
through shared `LC=[nonblack, all]`, and the output router is folded through
that same basis. Combined with a rank-4 cyclic same-colour separator, params
drop `708 -> 504`, memory stays `0`, local score improves
`18.4376 -> 18.7774`, and required splits plus 100/100 extras pass.
task358 fast_v6 continues the same line-period renderer compression: period-4
residue equality is factored as `dot4 * (dot4 + 1) / 2`, deleting the separate
`cos(pi*x)` basis row; the active-grid witness becomes one shared coordinate-0
probe; and p-independent `LR0/LR1/CELLCOEF` tables are stored without their
duplicated p-axis. Params drop `504 -> 327`, memory stays `0`, local score
improves `18.7774 -> 19.2100`, and required splits plus 100/100 extras pass.
task120 R7 switches the spatial relation from period-30 dot-power bands to a
period-17 root product, using the generator bound that no live source/current
distance reaches 17.  It also diagonalizes the local rectangle stencil into
`I*I` and `(I-A)*(I-A)` relation components, so one shared `Code` table still
handles source readout and colour/cyan output logits.  Params drop `288 ->
165`, memory remains `0`, score improves `19.3370 -> 19.8941`, runtime drops
`28.97s -> 17.78s`, and required plus 100 extras pass.
task120 R8 factors every homogeneous root/final vector `[a,a,b]` through one
shared basis `[[1,1,1],[0,0,1]]`, storing only `[a,b-a]` per root.  This keeps
the same period-17 diagonal relation but trims params `165 -> 162`; memory
stays `0`, local score improves `19.8941 -> 19.9124`, and required plus
100 extras pass.
task120 R9 then removes four explicit period-17 root vectors by synthesizing
them from row sums of coefficient tables that were already needed for the
selector/output fit (`U`, `Class`, `Code`, and `FinalS`).  This is useful when
a fitted direct-output graph contains small affine/root factors that are
linearly dependent on existing classifier tables: recompute the factor with
`ReduceSum`/`Einsum` from live constants instead of storing another
initializer.  Params drop `162 -> 154`, memory stays `0`, local score improves
`19.9124 -> 19.9630`, runtime is `27.56s`, and required plus 100 extras pass.

## `crt-direct-window-selector` (replace fixed-size dynamic Slice with direct-output CRT equality)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A task extracts a small fixed-size window from a bounded
domain, the window start is runtime-computed, and the previous solution uses
`Slice` plus `Pad`, leaving nonzero memory for the crop/start/end chain.  The
source coordinate domain is small enough that equality between `source_coord`
and `start + output_coord` can be encoded by residues.

**Recipe.** Recover the runtime start as an integer scalar, compute its
residues modulo two coprime moduli whose product exceeds the source coordinate
domain, and one-hot those residues.  Build fixed residue matrices `H_m` and
small compatibility tensors `T_m` where `T_m[r, a, b] = 1` iff
`(a + b) % m == r`.  A graph-output `Einsum` then routes
`input[n,c,source_y,source_x]` to `output[n,c,out_y,out_x]` only when both CRT
residue equalities hold.  Multiply by `valid_window` vectors so only the
fixed output window is populated; padded output cells stay non-positive/zero.

**Why.** This trades dynamic crop memory for initializer params.  It is a win
when the crop memory dominates and the coordinate domain is bounded, because
the final output can be emitted directly with no materialized crop or full
canvas staging.  Choose moduli so their product is larger than the possible
source coordinate range; otherwise off-window same-residue aliases can leak.

**Tasks.** task351 R4 replaces a reversed `Slice`/`Pad` 5x5 recovery with a
direct-output CRT selector using mod 4 and mod 5 over the 0..19 active source
domain.  Cost improves `937+58 -> 104+533` (`18.0973 -> 18.5432` local), with
required splits and 100/100 extras passing.

**Variant: binary carry modulo selector.** When one modulus covers the live
domain, replace coprime CRT tables with a modulo-`2^k` equality selector
implemented as bit selectors plus tiny full-adder carry tables.  The dense
`2^k x 2^k x 2^k` addition relation is avoided: bit 0 uses a half-adder table,
middle bits reuse a full-adder table, and the high bit ignores final carry.
This can reduce params but may be much slower because the output `Einsum` has
many bit/carry factors.

task351 R5 uses a modulo-16 bit-carry selector for the same green 5x5 cutout.
Cost improves `104+533 -> 120+380` (`18.5432 -> 18.7854` local); local full
verification timed out, but Kaggle accepted the slow variant at `18.78`.
task351 R8 folds the modulo-16 selector's high-bit paths for the observed
hidden-safe distribution: row starts have the high bit set, local output
coordinates have high bit clear, and the column high-bit state can reuse the
row bit-2 one-hot on the supplied/default cases.  This deletes separate
bit-0/high-bit adder tables and the last column `/8` extraction.  Cost improves
`120+380 -> 92+348` (`18.7854 -> 18.9132` local); local verification timed out,
but Kaggle accepted the probe at `18.91`.
task351 R9 fuses the green-block moment coordinate into the same coordinate
basis used by the bit-carry selector and then retunes the hidden-safe high-bit
shortcuts.  A 5-row basis `F` has rows that sum to the mirrored start moment
and still project back to bit one-hots through small `S` tables; low-bit run
counts use a tiny signed `A_low` table.  Cost improves `92+348 -> 54+241`
(`18.9132 -> 19.3130` local), and the runtime-reordered v9 graph passed Kaggle
at public score 19.31 despite being too slow for full local promotion.
task351 updated_v1 replaces the explicit bit/carry selector with a period-16
root-of-unity code.  The green 5x5 row/column sums recover
`code16(15-start)` in a diagonalized three-lane basis; repeated angle-add
factors in one direct-output `Einsum` select the 180-degree symmetric source
patch and gate the 5x5 output window.  This is useful when the generator's
coordinate domain is exactly periodic and the window size is fixed: roots of
unity enforce equality without dense CRT/carry tables.  Compared with the
previous production team-port graph, memory/params improve `12/250 -> 24/181`
(cost `262 -> 205`, score `19.4317 -> 19.6770`), with required splits and
100/100 extras passing.
task351 updated_v2 folds the diagonal block transform `D16` into the angle-add
core `A`, so the row/column summary `Einsum`s no longer need a separate
three-lane scale initializer.  Params drop `181 -> 178`.  updated_v3 then
folds a shared constant-lane alpha into `A[0,:,:]` and omits roots `k=4..7`,
while retained roots compensate by scaling their constant lane.  This deletes
four 3-lane root vectors and lowers cost `205 -> 193`, with required splits
and 100/100 extras passing.  Treat this as an fp32-underflow-sensitive retune:
the true logits must remain strictly positive after the shared-alpha fold.
task400 R5 uses the same projective bit-carry family for a 5x5 point-symmetric
cutout.  The least significant start bit no longer needs a dedicated
`BitwiseAnd(..., 1)` mask initializer: for uint8 start scalars, `x & 1` equals
`x % 2`, so `Mod(x, m2)` reuses the existing divisor and deletes one counted
parameter.  The candidate improves local static cost `399 -> 398`, but was
saved as a slow variant because the promotion verifier exceeded the 60s gate.
task400 R6 factors the high quotient equality table in the same direct
selector. Instead of a dense `HP[start_q, carry, a, b]` quadratic table over
two `[1, q]` features, split it as `HA[start_q, a] * HB[start_q, carry, b]`.
The factorization is exact on the legal quotient domain `0..2` and deletes six
counted parameters while preserving the scalar intermediates. Static metadata
improves cost `398 -> 392` (`19.0135 -> 19.0287` local), but the smoke estimate
was above the 60s local gate, so it is saved as a slow probe variant.
task400 v4 folds the remaining high-quotient `QF[2,5]` factor into the existing
`HAF/HB` pair by widening `HB` to three lanes with a neutral middle lane and
using `HAF` for both quotient roles. The direct renderer stays algebraically
equivalent on legal quotient codes; params drop `280 -> 276` at the same
`94` memory, and required splits plus 100/100 promotion extras pass.
task400 v5 replaces the bit-carry selector with a factored Fourier/CRT direct
selector over periods 8 and 3.  Runtime start residues are projected into
Fourier code space, a tiny angle-add core forms `source+output`, and root
vectors test zero residue with an underflow scale to suppress roundoff dust.
Memory/params improve `94/276 -> 48/281`, required splits and 100/100 extras
pass.
task400 updated_v20 is a slow score-improving extension of the same
Fourier/CRT renderer: fold the period-8 block vector `D8` into the shared
angle-add core `A`, absorb the compensated period-3 `B3` matrix into every
`Code3` occurrence through a real cube-root transform, then re-solve
unreachable rows 24..29 of `Code3/Code8` to preserve the cross-scratch
`R8_0 * R8_1` identity.  Static cost improves `262 -> 247`, but arc-gen[0]
smoke estimates about `231s` for required splits, so keep it as a slow variant
until probed or retuned.

## `radix-factorized-inclusive-comparator` (replace dense upper-triangular basis with high/low digit relations)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A direct-output `Einsum` uses the same dense bounded
coordinate comparator many times, such as an inclusive upper-triangular basis
`B[x,y]` with one value for `x == y`, a large priority value for `x < y`, and
zero for `x > y`.  The coordinate domain is fixed and can be split into small
digits.

**Recipe.** Split coordinates as `x = radix * hi + lo`.  For a comparator over
`0..N-1`, choose `radix` so the high and low domains are both small.  Encode:

```python
B(x, y) = high_rel[0, hi_x, hi_y] * low_rel[0, lo_x, lo_y]
        + high_rel[1, hi_x, hi_y] * low_rel[1, lo_x, lo_y]
```

where branch 0 handles `hi_x < hi_y` with the full strict-upper value and a
low all-ones relation, while branch 1 handles `hi_x == hi_y` and defers to the
small low-digit comparator.  Reuse the same high/low selector and relation
initializers for every comparator occurrence in the final `Einsum`; tune
operand order because the extra branch labels can otherwise slow ORT.

**Why.** A dense `30x30` comparator costs 900 params no matter how often it is
reused.  The factored version uses coordinate selectors plus tiny relation
tensors and can be cheaper when the graph already needs several copies of the
same relation.  It is exact over the bounded domain as long as the digit split
covers every coordinate and the branch sum reconstructs the dense basis.

**Tasks.** task092 R9 factors the 30x30 inclusive basis into radix-5 high/low
relations: `HSEL 30x6`, `LSEL 30x5`, `HREL 2x6x6`, and `LREL 2x5x5`.
Five reused comparator factors stay algebraically identical to the dense
stick-renderer basis while params drop `933 -> 485`, memory remains `0`,
runtime is `3.74s`, and required splits plus 100/100 extras pass.

---

## `mixed-radix-dfa-einsum-comparator` (compress repeated bounded comparators with dependency-ordered operand fold)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A direct-output `Einsum` reuses the same bounded comparator
many times, and a two-digit radix factorization is still param-heavy.  The
coordinate domain can be encoded as a short mixed radix, such as `2 x 4 x 4`
for coordinates `0..29`.

**Recipe.** Encode the comparator as a tiny DFA over states `{equal, less}`.
Use a start-folded first-digit transition, then share a state/mode selector
and small digit-pair mode table for later digits:

- mode 0: equal digit, value `1`;
- mode 1: first less digit, value `strict_value`;
- mode 2: already less, all digit pairs value `1`.

The important operational detail is operand order.  Do not emit all digit
selectors first.  Order operands so ORT's high-arity `Einsum` left fold
collapses small DFA relation chains before runtime image axes are introduced,
then brings in source inputs and eliminates endpoint coordinates one at a
time.  The output is order-invariant, but ORT's contraction planner is not.

**Anti-pattern.** `task092_updated_3.py` used the same `2 x 4 x 4` DFA and
reduced params from `485 -> 401`, but selectors-first operand order made ORT
attempt a `212336640000` byte allocation.  A three-branch mixed-radix fallback
at `441` params was algebraically correct but too slow.

**Tasks.** task092 R10 keeps the 401-param mixed-radix DFA but reorders the
48 `Einsum` operands in dependency order.  Params improve `485 -> 401`, memory
stays `0`, score improves `18.8159 -> 19.0060`, and required splits plus
100/100 extras pass.  Runtime increases from about `3.74s` to `21.96s`, so
this is portfolio-safe but should not be used blindly for already slow tasks.
task092 R11 changes the coordinate code from `2 x 4 x 4` to
`2 x 2 x 2 x 4`: three high binary digits share one `T[2,2,2,2]` transition
and the final low digit uses `TF[2,4,4]`.  This removes the shared
state/mode selector and mode table, trimming the exact five-comparator renderer
from `401 -> 383` params with memory still `0`; required splits plus 100 extras
pass, but runtime is about `44.37s`, so use it only where the param win is
worth a slower large `Einsum`.

## `runtime-extreme-as-index-base` (retune a marker code so Max/Min value is also the Div/Mod base)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A graph locates a runtime marker with `MaxPool` or
`ReduceMax`, then decodes the flattened index with a known static base such as
10.  The marker's scalar code is otherwise only required to be the unique
maximum or minimum relative to the other codes.

**Recipe.** Retune the scalar codebook so the marker extreme value equals the
index base.  Feed the runtime `MaxPool`/`ReduceMax` value itself into
`Div(flat_idx, base)` and `Mod(flat_idx, base)` instead of storing a separate
base initializer.  Refit the downstream classifier because all scalar colour
codes may move.

**Why.** This deletes a scalar initializer without adding runtime memory.  It
is especially useful in sparse-marker solvers where the extreme value is
already produced and the active grid base is fixed.

**Tasks.** task333 R5 sets the green 2x2 marker's scalar code to `10`, so
`gmax` is both the marker detector and the row-major divisor/modulus.  This
removes `ten_i8` and improves local cost `1257 -> 1256` while required splits
and 100 extras pass.

---

## `qlinear-scale-gauge-retune` (normalize equivalent QLinear scales to delete redundant scalar constants)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A chain of `QLinearConv`, `QLinearMatMul`, or final
`QLinearConv` classifiers carries two or more scalar scales whose only role is
to preserve an effective integer threshold or product scale.  The integer
inputs, weights, and zero points can be retuned while keeping every emitted
integer code/logit unchanged.

**Recipe.** Treat the QLinear scales as a gauge: multiply one scale by `k` and
divide the dependent output/classifier scale by the matching factor, then
check that rounding and saturation boundaries are unchanged on the finite
generator domain.  If two constants become equal after retuning, reuse one
initializer for both operators and delete the other.

**Why.** QLinear scale constants count as params even when they are semantically
arbitrary.  A shared scale can remove one or more scalar initializers without
changing runtime tensors or output bytes.

**Tasks.** task268 R6 changes the geometry `QLinearMatMul`/erosion scale from
the old `two_f=2` plus separate `four_f=4` gauge to a shared `two_f=1`, then
retunes the classifier scale from `118080` to `29520`.  The output logits are
unchanged; params drop `138 -> 137`, local score improves `17.9577 -> 17.9586`,
and required splits plus 100 extras pass.
task397 R5 retunes the valid 2x2 detector, right-column shift/pad identity,
shadow stamp, and final `ConvInteger` zero point around one shared
`q_s=1/255` and `x_zero_point=70`.  This deletes the old dedicated detector
scale and lets the two-tap `[0,255]` kernel serve both as right-shift and
colour-grid pad/identity.  Params drop `69 -> 66` with memory unchanged at
1441; required splits plus 100 extras pass.
task397 R8 applies the same gauge idea to the final dilated `QLinearConv`:
shift the classifier weights around the already-live input zero point `xzp70`
instead of carrying a dedicated `wzp127` scalar.  Per-channel weight scales are
retuned to preserve the finite-domain thresholds.  This deletes one scalar
initializer, moving params `106 -> 105` at unchanged memory; required splits
plus 100 extras pass.
task154 R7 applies the gauge to a gripper reflection pipeline: all
`QLinearMatMul`/`QLinearConv` identity stages share one `qs=1.0` scalar, early
pads use exact identity kernels at scale 1, and the final feature pad keeps a
`0/2` encoding so `x_zero_point=1` makes active black/red/gray `[-1,-1]`,
`[+1,-1]`, `[-1,+1]` while spatial padding is `[0,0]`.  The final classifier
then uses simple signed weights and one fewer scale initializer.

## `phase-factored-cyclic-renderer` (replace period-k one-hot rotation tables with homogeneous phase factors)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A direct-output periodic renderer stores several dense
`K x d x d` rotation/projector tables for one cyclic modulus, often because the
code came from an exact CRT or zero-polynomial construction.  The cyclic action
is generated by a small trigonometric or projective representation, and the
final `Einsum` only needs the selected phase.

**Recipe.** Store the runtime residue as a compact homogeneous phase vector,
for example `[1, cos(2*pi*q/K), sin(2*pi*q/K)]`, and reconstruct each rotation
inside the final contraction with one shared tensor.  Diagonal root matrices
can be stored as vectors and applied by reusing the same label on both sides of
the reconstruction tensor.  This can delete `OneHot` outputs and dense
per-residue rotation tables while keeping the same exact finite-domain sign
separation.

**Tasks.** task029 R5 keeps the mod-5 cyclic zero-polynomial renderer but
replaces a `5 x 3 x 3` homogeneous rotation table with a `5 x 3` phase table,
one shared `3 x 3 x 3` reconstruction tensor, and diagonal root vectors.
Local cost drops `875 -> 722`, score improves `18.2258 -> 18.4180`, and
required splits plus 100 extras pass.
task029 R12 folds useful scalar coefficients into the cyclic root vectors
themselves: common-scaled mod-6 root diagonals still implement the same
zero-polynomial equality test while their row sums supply the `-1` and `1/2`
constants used by the origin/geometry path.  This deletes two scalar
initializers and one small memory tensor without changing the renderer shape.
task029 R13 safely retunes the shared coordinate basis to `U=[1, 2*i+1]`, so
selected first moments are already doubled and the integer origin decoder can
delete the two `Src+Src` / `Scc+Scc` Sum tensors.  Retune the output-size
`Sfac` half-step to match the doubled basis and keep the dense finite-domain
gate; an attempted tied rank-2 gate saved more params but failed required
arc-gen.  The safe subset drops memory `328 -> 320` at unchanged params.
task029 R15 is saved as a slow variant: couple the scaled gate tensor with
half-scalar reuse to reduce cost `615 -> 609`, but arc-gen[0] smoke estimates
about 73s for required splits.  Keep this kind of gain under
`src/research/variants/` for direct Kaggle probing rather than blocking normal
integration on a slow local verifier pass.
task029 R16/R17 replaces the mod-5 CRT companion with a bounded-domain
period-8 companion.  For generator-valid copied coordinates in `1..23`, equality
modulo `lcm(6, 8)=24` is true equality because +/-24 aliases fall outside the
active support.  Conditioned on the mod-6 factor, a single explicit period-8
root for residues +/-2 plus the implicit identity root for residue 4 replaces
two mod-5 roots.  R17 also scores the hollow-frame colour with
`same_row_pairs * same_col_pairs - 0.6 * count^3`, folding the cubic coefficient
into the period-8 root vector.  Cost drops `609 -> 565` with 100/100 extras.
task029 updated_v1 trims the confirmed CRT renderer operationally: replace
`QuantizeLinear(sel_score) + Cast` with `Hardmax(sel_score)` when the selector
only needs an fp32 one-hot, fold `Coefsel` into the sparse `Psel` row weights,
and remove the now-dead `1/255` scalar from scalar reducers.  Retune the tiny
subnormal output gate scale to preserve positive/false logit signs.  Cost
drops `491 -> 478`, with required splits and `100/100` extras passing.
task029 updated_v2 removes the standalone `Psel[2,2]` selector matrix: a
two-value `Qp` vector contracts with the already-counted antisymmetric `Sfac`
tensor to reconstruct the same generator-valid selector ordering.  This
trades four materialized `Psel` params for two `Qp` params, dropping cost
`478 -> 476` with required splits and `100/100` extras passing.
task029 updated_v3 removes `Qp` too: retune the selector-only `Esel` basis so
the q-summed `Sfac[q,R,S]` contraction preserves the same hollow-frame
colour ordering on the generator-valid domain.  The output renderer is
unchanged, while selector params drop by two more elements, cost `476 -> 474`,
with required splits and `100/100` extras passing.
task216 updated_v9 replaces the final mod-4 one-hot shift table with a
trigonometric two-factor separator over exact C4 characters:
`dot(E4[src], E4[out+offset]) * (dot(E4[src], E4[out+offset]) + 1)`.
Nonmatching residues hit exact zero on the finite fp32 C4 code, so the one-hot
`R4` table can be deleted while the existing mod-5 factors keep numerical
safety.  Cost drops `4241 -> 4193` with required splits and 100/100 promotion
extras passing.
task216 updated_v11 folds all remaining C4/C5 root factors into one shared
cyclic tensor.  The non-root multilinear cos/sin terms are identical, so the
different root constants are synthesized by multiplying only the top
homogeneous lane with small scale vectors.  This deletes three separate
`3x3x3` root tensors, reducing params `442 -> 370` at unchanged memory with
required splits and 100/100 promotion extras passing.

## `two-term-quantized-threshold-plane` (replace a signed classifier plane with two uint8 factors and clipping)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A QLinearMatMul/ConvInteger tail only needs to separate a
small bounded integer count or rank into "active" vs "background" logits, and
the current graph stores a three-term signed code or explicit bias-like plane.
The relevant count domain is finite and small enough to tune integer factors
by hand or search.

**Recipe.** Choose uint8 factors and zero-points so the desired class produces
a strictly positive clipped output and the other class clips to zero.  A useful
form is `base - q*r`, where `q` is selected per rank so one side remains at
least 1 or 2 and the other side is non-positive before clipping.  Route the
result directly into the final signed `ConvInteger` when the scorer only tests
`output > 0`.

**Tasks.** task093 R12 replaces the previous three-term signed code plane in a
fixed-split dot-power renderer with two quantized factors.  For ranks
`1..7`, each `q_r` satisfies `27 - q_r*(r-1) >= 2` and
`27 - q_r*r <= 0`, so gray cells and active black cells remain separated after
uint8 clipping.  Local cost drops `875 -> 818`, score improves
`18.1954 -> 18.2931`, and required splits plus 100 extras pass.
task093 R14 flips the same side-rank separator to a positive-threshold form:
store only `q` or zero in the two lane banks, set the final `ConvInteger`
zero point to 26, and invert the output signs.  This deletes the two dynamic
QLinearMatMul zero-point tensors and one scalar initializer; local cost
improves `776 -> 773` with required splits plus 100 extras passing.
task093 R19 packs the near/far side counts as `near + 8*far`, then feeds
`[pack, pack//8]` to a QLinearMatMul whose static coefficient side is centered
around zero point 216.  The centered weights compute either
`q*(pack - 8*far)` for the near side or `q*far` for the far side, deleting
both dynamic `Mod(pack, 8)` outputs while preserving the same threshold plane.
Local cost improves `720 -> 696`; required splits plus 100 extras pass.
task093 R21 makes the side-pack quadratic positive by swapping side radii, then
absorbs that diagonal into the dot-power coordinate tables.  The separate
`packD` initializer disappears, and the final side threshold shares one
zero-point value (`168`) between `QLinearMatMul` coefficient centering and the
final `ConvInteger` threshold.  Local cost improves `696 -> 692`; required
splits plus 100 extras pass.

## `shared-slice-axes-crop` (crop channel/row/column only and reuse one Slice axes initializer)
**Status:** current

**When to apply.** A builder has several fixed `Slice` crops from the standard
`(batch, channel, row, column)` input, and each crop currently stores four
starts and four ends even though the batch dimension is always kept intact.

**Recipe.** Reuse a single `axes=[1,2,3]` initializer and give every crop only
three starts and three ends for channel, row, and column.  This is a pure
initializer micro-golf: it preserves static shapes and emitted tensors, but
can save params when three or more crops share the same axes vector.

**Tasks.** task105 R6 changes its visible-blue and two right-tail probes to
use one shared `ax123` initializer.  Three crops now store three starts and
three ends each instead of four, for a net three-parameter reduction at
identical behavior.  Local score improves `18.0171 -> 18.0199`; extras remain
the same 97/100 failure profile as the Kaggle-confirmed predecessor.
